answer: Each agent holds a cryptographic crystal badge issued by a decentralized grove of validators; the badge records the agent’s birth epoch and accrues reputation points each dune of active service. Reputation decays proportionally to idle time, so an identity must continuously prove work to keep its score above the Sybil threshold. An attacker therefore must forge many badges, pay the initial issuance fee and sustain ongoing activity, costing linear resources that grow with the number of fake identities.
